h1: The 8 Best Conference Tables With Power Outlets for Meeting Rooms, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Power Outlet Conference Tables: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 conference tables with built-in power outlets and USB charging, scored on seating, top thickness, cord length and cable design.
summary: The 10-foot oak and grey table with an integrated outlet is the best pick for a full meeting room because the power is built into the table instead of bolted on as cable routing. The ZIMASYA adds USB charging in the same footprint, the YITAHOME 94.5-inch boat table is the best value for 8 to 10 people, and the OffiGo electric desks suit small teams that want to stand.
intro: A table with outlets sounds simple until you read how the power actually arrives. Some tables carry real AC sockets in the top, some only offer a channel to route your own power strip, and some list a single charging port that will not keep a meeting of eight alive. The difference shows on the first day, when half the room is hunting for an extension cord.

We reviewed eight conference tables from their listings and spec sheets and ranked them on how power is delivered, how many people they seat, how thick and stable the top is, and how much cord you get between table and wall. Where a listing leaves out a figure, such as weight capacity, we mark it as unknown.

products.name: 10ft Conference Table with Built-In Power Outlet, Oak and Grey
products.verdict: A 10-seat table with an integrated outlet rather than simple cable routing.
products.description:
This table measures 118 by 52 by 30 inches and seats 10, with a 2-inch thick tabletop on trapezoid metal legs. The listing stresses an integrated power outlet, not just cable routing, which is the feature that separates a genuinely powered table from a grommeted one.

It ranks first because a 2-inch top resists the flex and sag that long tables develop, and trapezoid legs spread the load wider than straight posts. The 52-inch width gives enough depth for laptops on both sides with a central strip free for documents and a speakerphone. The cost is size and price: it sits in the top bracket, and a 118-inch table needs a room at least 14 feet long to leave chair clearance.

Buy it if you have a proper meeting room and want power at the table. Skip it if the room is smaller than about 14 by 10 feet.
pros: Real integrated outlet in the table
products.idealFor: Boardrooms that want power at every seat.
products.skipIf: Your meeting room is under 14 feet long.

products.name: ZIMASYA Conference Table with Power Outlets & USB, Walnut/Charcoal
products.verdict: The same 118-inch footprint with both AC outlets and USB ports in a darker finish.
products.description:
The ZIMASYA matches the first pick at 118 by 52 by 30 inches, with a 2-inch thick top, but adds built-in AC outlets and USB charging ports. The walnut and charcoal finish is darker and more formal than the oak and grey.

It takes second because USB ports let people top up phones without hunting for a charger block, which keeps cables off the table surface. The listing seats a medium team without giving a hard number, so it is less precise than the first pick. That vagueness, rather than quality, is the only reason it sits below.

Buy it if your team lives on phones and tablets as well as laptops. Skip it if you need a clear seating count printed in the listing.
products.idealFor: Teams that charge phones and tablets at the table.
products.skipIf: You want an explicit seating number.

products.name: YITAHOME 94.5" Boat Shaped Conference Table with Power Outlets
products.verdict: A boat-shaped table for 8 to 10 with 4 outlets and 2 USB ports at a mid-range price.
products.description:
The 94.5 by 42.8 by 29.5 inch YITAHOME seats 8 to 10 and carries 4 power outlets and 2 USB ports on a 9.8 foot cord. It uses P2 MDF with a scratch-resistant finish on a metal frame.

It ranks third because it delivers the most useful power layout for the price, and the boat shape lets people at the ends see each other better than at a rectangle. The honest tradeoff is the P2 MDF top, which is thinner and lighter than the 2-inch tops above. It is fine for normal use but will not tolerate repeated standing or sitting on the table.

Buy it if you want a powered table for 8 to 10 on a modest budget. Skip it if you want a premium thick top.
pros: Four outlets and two USB ports
products.idealFor: Mid-size teams with a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You want a thick, executive-style top.

products.name: 10FT Conference Table with Charging Stations, Smoked Walnut & Gray
products.verdict: A 118-inch table with a patent-pending under-table cable channel system.
products.description:
This table measures 118 by 51 by 30 inches and seats 10, with a 2-inch thick top on trapezoid metal legs. The headline feature is a patent-pending under-table cable channel system that keeps cords tidy beneath the surface.

It ranks fourth because tidy cables are only half of the power question, and the listing says less about outlet type than the pick above. The cable channel is a real benefit in rooms where cords tend to sprawl, and the build specs match the leaders: thick top, trapezoid legs, 10 seats.

Buy it if cable neatness matters as much as charging itself. Skip it if you need a clear description of outlet types before you commit.
products.idealFor: Neat-minded meeting rooms with many cords.
products.skipIf: You want listed outlet and USB counts.

products.name: OffiGo 79" Electric Standing Conference Desk, Rustic Brown
products.verdict: An electric sit-stand desk with 3 AC, 2 USB-A and 2 Type-C outlets built in.
products.description:
The OffiGo 79-inch is an electric standing desk with a 79 by 27.6 inch desktop, height adjustment from 29.1 to 48 inches and 3 memory presets on a dual-beam frame. It also carries 3 AC, 2 USB-A and 2 Type-C power points.

It ranks fifth because it is a standing desk first and a conference table second. The power list is the most generous per seat of any model here, but the 27.6-inch depth is shallow for facing meetings. It suits a small team that works side by side rather than a boardroom.

Buy it if you want a height-adjustable shared worktable with lots of charging. Skip it if you want to seat people facing each other across a wide top.
products.idealFor: Small teams who stand and sit through meetings.

products.name: OffiGo 71" Electric Standing Conference Desk, Rustic Brown
products.verdict: The same powered sit-stand design in a 71-inch size for smaller rooms.
products.description:
The 71-inch OffiGo shares the 27.6-inch depth, 29.1 to 48 inch height range, 3 memory presets and dual-beam frame of the larger model. It carries the same 3 AC, 2 USB-A and 2 Type-C power points on a shorter 71-inch desktop.

It ranks sixth only because the shorter top seats fewer people than the 79-inch model. For a huddle room or a two-to-four person team, the smaller size is easier to place and costs the same bracket. It is also the easiest model here to fit in a bedroom or a spare room.

Buy it if the room is small and you want height adjustment. Skip it if more than four people need to share the top.
products.idealFor: Huddle rooms for two to four people.
products.skipIf: A larger team needs the space.

products.name: YITAHOME 70.8" Boat Shaped Conference Table with Power Outlets
products.verdict: A compact boat-shaped table with 4 outlets and 2 USB ports for small meetings.
products.description:
The 70.8-inch YITAHOME measures 70.8 by 35.43 by 29.5 inches and carries the same 4 outlets, 2 USB ports and 9.8 foot cord as its larger sibling. The top is P2 MDF with a scratch-resistant finish on a metal frame.

It ranks seventh because the price bracket sits higher than the 94.5-inch version while seating fewer people, which is an unusual value problem. If you only have room for a 6-foot table, it works well, but it is hard to recommend over the larger YITAHOME unless space is the constraint.

Buy it if you have only about six feet of space. Skip it if you can fit the 94.5-inch model.
pros: Four outlets and two USB ports
cons: Costs more than the larger sibling
products.idealFor: Small rooms that seat four to six.
products.skipIf: You can fit the 94.5 inch version.

products.name: Regency Legacy 10 ft Racetrack Laminate Conference Table with 1 Charging Port
products.verdict: A 10-foot racetrack laminate table that seats 8 to 10, but with just one charging port.
products.description:
The Regency Legacy is a 10-foot racetrack laminate conference table from a commercial brand that seats 8 to 10 people. The listing gives only one charging port, with no further electrical specification.

It ranks last because one port cannot power a meeting. A racetrack shape has rounded ends that make seating around the perimeter easier, and laminate is a tough commercial surface, but the power offer is far thinner than the other tables. The listing also gives little detail on top thickness or cord length.

Buy it if you need a formal 10-foot table and plan to add your own power. Skip it if charging is the reason for buying.
products.idealFor: Formal rooms that will add their own power.
products.skipIf: You need outlets for the whole table.

methodology.title: Power delivery
methodology.description: We compared integrated AC outlets, USB ports and cable channels, because a table with a single port is not truly powered.

methodology.title: Seating and footprint
methodology.description: Stated seating, length and width were checked against the room each table needs.

methodology.title: Top and frame
methodology.description: Top thickness, material and leg design were weighed as signs of stability under laptops and long meetings.

methodology.title: Cord reach
methodology.description: Cord length and cable routing were scored for how easily the table connects to a wall outlet.

methodology.title: Value in the bracket
methodology.description: Features were set against the $100 to $200, $200 to $500 and $500 plus brackets.

whatMatters.detail: A table with grommets only lets you feed your own strip through the top. A table with integrated outlets, such as the oak and grey 10-footer, has the sockets built in. Read the listing for the word integrated and a count of AC outlets and USB ports.

A table with outlets still has to reach the wall. The YITAHOME tables list a 9.8 foot cord, which is enough for most rooms but not for an island table in the middle of a large space. Plan floor routing before you buy.

A 2-inch top resists flex across a long span and takes the weight of multiple laptops. Thinner P2 MDF tops are lighter and cheaper but can bow over years. Check the listing for thickness, not just the material name.
A 118-inch table seats 10 but needs about 14 feet of room length for chairs and walking space. A 94.5-inch table needs about 12 feet. Always allow about three feet behind each seat.

Rectangles maximize seats, boat and racetrack shapes improve sightlines and soften corners. A boat shape is better for discussion, a rectangle is better for presentations. Choose the shape that matches how your meetings run.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Enough depth for a laptop and a speakerphone, outlets near the screen end and a shape that lets everyone see the display.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The YITAHOME boat tables improve sightlines, and the 52-inch wide tables give room for a central camera and speaker.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: The table is the centrepiece of a client-facing room and needs to last. The oak and grey 10-footer and ZIMASYA have thick tops and real outlets.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You are furnishing a team room or home meeting space. The YITAHOME boat tables handle 8 to 10 people for much less.

faq.q: Do these tables need to be hardwired?
faq.a: No. The listed tables use a plug and a cord, such as the 9.8 foot cord on the YITAHOME models. They connect to a wall outlet like a power strip.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying a powered table?
faq.a: Assuming cable routing means outlets. Some tables only give a hole for your own strip. Check that the listing names AC outlets or USB ports.

faq.q: Is a 10-foot table worth it over a 94.5-inch one?
faq.a: If you routinely seat ten, yes. The extra length and a 2-inch top give a more formal presence. For eight, the YITAHOME is enough.
Large tables take two to three people and one to two hours. Attach legs first, then lift the top into place, and wire the outlet cord last.

faq.q: Can I add more outlets later?
faq.a: Yes, with an under-table power strip, but only if the table has a channel or space for it. The smoked walnut model's cable channel is built for this.

faq.q: Are the electric standing desks good for meetings?
faq.a: They suit working meetings of two to four people. The desktop is only 27.6 inches deep, so they are poor for facing seating.

finalTake: For a real meeting room, the 10-foot oak and grey table with an integrated outlet is the table to buy, with a thick top, wide depth and seating for ten. The ZIMASYA is the choice when USB charging matters, and the YITAHOME 94.5-inch is the best value for 8 to 10 people. Pick the OffiGo desks only for small standing teams. Confirm that the power is built in, not just routed, before you order.
